page: Google Cloud Platform n4-highmem-2 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance configured with 2 vCPUs and 16.0 GB of RAM. This configuration yields a memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. The instance is powered by an Intel x86_64 processor with 1 physical core and 2 threads per core, utilizing dedicated CPU allocation. The processor features a cache hierarchy consisting of 48 KB L1d, 2 MB L2, and 260 MB L3 cache. It supports advanced instruction sets including Intel Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX, AVX512f, AVX512_VNNI, AVX_VNNI, AVX512_BF16) and Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX_TILE, AMX_INT8), alongside cryptographic acceleration via AES, VAES, and SHA_NI. No local storage or complimentary public IPv4 addresses are bundled with this instance.

Performance benchmarks indicate average single-core capabilities but notable multi-core and memory bandwidth limitations. Single-core stress-ng and Geekbench scores fall into the average category, supported by average single-threaded performance in gzip compression and bzip3 decompression. However, multi-core benchmarks, such as stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core, are rated poor and weak respectively, reflecting the physical single-core limitation. Memory bandwidth tests for both small and large blocks show poor performance, with large block read-only bandwidth at 15.05 GB/sec and write bandwidth at 9.22 GB/sec. Database operations and Redis SET operations also register in the poor performance tier, with Redis achieving 2.24 million operations per second.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the n4-highmem-2 offers an entry-point into memory-optimized workloads without the expense of high-core-count instances. However, the trade-off is constrained multi-threaded processing and lower memory throughput. This instance is best suited for low-throughput memory-bound workloads, basic text processing, single-threaded utility scripts, or lightweight development environments that require more RAM than standard general-purpose instances but do not demand high parallel processing power or intensive database transaction rates.
